question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0$, $x=2$, $y=0$, $y=2$, $z=0$, $z=1$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(4x^{2})\,i+(xyz)\,j+(6y)\,k$, the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(6y) \\  & =8x+xz+0 \\  & =xz+8x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(xz+8x)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,xz+8x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
